summary: Streaming output freeze during inflight batch resynchronization causing mid-generation disconnects
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports streaming chat sessions (SSE) freezing mid-generation for ~5-30s and then either resuming partial output or aborting with a 499/connection-reset. This started after a platform change to adaptive batching heuristics rolled 2026-03-12 UTC.

Impact: Intermittent live chat interruptions for NimbusHealth clients during high-concurrency bursts; user-visible broken assistant responses and several support tickets opened. Estimated ~3% of long-stream requests in us-east during peak show the symptom.

Environment: prod/us-east, Dedicated pool "nimbus-dedicated-01"
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use SSE-based chat endpoint with user message that triggers ~800-1200 token response.
2) Simulate burst of concurrent requests (50-100) to the same model variant within a 30s window.
3) Observe SSE stream: after initial tokens, stream becomes silent for 5-30s.
4) Either stream resumes with a block of tokens or connection resets.

(We reproduced reliably when adaptive_batch_window < 30ms and when worker rebinds occurred.)
logs:
Selected log excerpts (sanitized):
- request_id=rid-7f3b, trace=tr-11a: chunk_emit at t=0.12s, last_chunk at t=0.84s, then no chunks until t=24.3s.
- worker=pool-3/worker-21: 'batch-resync initiated' at 2026-03-12T23:41:02Z; 'kv-cache-evict start' at 23:41:02.223; 'inflight-split lock' acquired.
- scheduler: 'adaptive_batch_respin: triggered for model gpt-4o-mini-v2, reason=latency_skew'
- tcp: FIN from client at 2026-03-12T23:41:27Z; upstream reset from worker at 23:41:27.310

Attached metrics: SSE_chunk_interval_p50/p95 spiked from 40ms/120ms to 1.2s/18.4s during windows correlated with autoscaler events and worker respins.
investigation_notes:
Chronology: Customer reported 2026-03-12 23:50 UTC. Support triaged and escalated to SRE and Serving team. We reproduced in staging by replaying burst traffic and toggling adaptive_batch_window.

Hypotheses considered:
- 1) Network intermediary (corporate proxy) buffering: unlikely — multiple customers and internal smoke tests show same pattern.
- 2) Application-level keepalive missing: keepalives present but behavior persists.
- 3) Adaptive batching/resynchronization (batch-respin) causes worker to serialise inflight batches, evict KV cache, and block chunk emission until kernel warm-up completes — this matches timing and 'kv-cache-evict' logs seen.
- 4) Preemption/noisy neighbor: some worker eviction noted but not enough to explain ~3% frequency.

Key evidence: 'batch-resync initiated' log aligns with silence start; p95 token emit gap ~18s matches worker re-init path (quantized kernel load + KV refill). Reproduced by forcing a batch-resync during inflight generation in staging.

Temporary mitigation tested: disabling adaptive_batch_respin eliminated the long-silence in the reproduction scenario but increased average latency slightly under heavy load.
comments: 2026-03-12 23:58 - Priya Nandakumar (Support): Notified customer and requested sample request_ids and timestamps. Asked for HTTP request headers and whether any proxy sits in front of clients.

2026-03-13 01:05 - NimbusHealth (Customer): Provided request_ids rid-7f3b, rid-91c0 and confirmed use of native SSE client behind enterprise load-balancer. Reported 12 impacted sessions during window.

2026-03-13 03:22 - Marco DeLuca (SRE): Reproduced in staging with adaptive_batch_respin enabled. Observed 'inflight-split lock' and prolonged token pause matching customer timings. Opening INT ticket to track runtime change. (INT-5512)

2026-03-13 09:40 - Engineering (Serving): PR created to add diagnostics around batch-resync and to emit a metric 'batch_resync_inflight_count' (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4382). Will also experiment with prewarming quantized kernels on resync path.

2026-03-14 02:17 - Priya Nandakumar (Support): Informed NimbusHealth of a temporary configuration to disable adaptive batch-respin on their dedicated pool; asked permission for limited rollback. Customer approved.
2026-03-14 05:00 - NimbusHealth (Customer): Confirmed immediate improvement after disabling resync — streams no longer freeze but a small latency increase observed in throughput-heavy bursts.
resolution:
Workaround applied: Disabled adaptive_batch_respin for NimbusHealth's dedicated pool (nimbus-dedicated-01) at 2026-03-14 05:03 UTC — observed immediate reduction of silent windows and no aborts in subsequent 2-hour smoke test.

Planned fix: Engineering to implement non-blocking resync path: prewarm quantized kernels before evicting KV cache, stream chunk flush policy to avoid silence during resync, and expose 'resync_grace_period' knob per-customer. Target: patch and canary 2026-03-21.

Follow-ups:
- Add alert for batch_resync_inflight_count > 0 with associated SSE_chunk_interval spikes.
- Postmortem to document exact timeline and rollouts; link INT-5512 for internal runtime change.
- Communicate to affected customers recommended config: increase adaptive_batch_window or disable resync until patch is live.

Status: Mitigated (workaround applied). Engineering in progress on code change. Expected full resolution by 2026-03-21.
notes: This ticket ties to the recent adaptive-batching rollout (2026-03-12). Keep customer informed of timeline and test patch in staging with their traffic profile before full rollout.
